The meeting itself was about the parks and recreation budget. The council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended version of that line item. A spokesperson for the mayor's office said the new number reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, but wouldn't say what those conversations actually covered.

Two council staffers pointed to a separate memo from the finance subcommittee that puts the adjustment at around $340,000. A budget analyst who looked it over called that figure "in the range we expected."

Now, back to that bridge. It's been sitting on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has racked up 14 change orders along the way. Despite the crack, nobody discussed the project in any detail during the meeting.

Council member Dana Okafor, asked about it afterward, kept things vague: "The process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
